patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient's family reports a gradual change in behavior starting a few months ago, which includes inappropriate laughing, using foul language, and occasionally grabbing people without warning. Recently, the patient's memory has also notably deteriorated, leading to difficulty in caring for himself.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Change in behavior including inappropriate actions
Secondary_Symptoms: Trouble taking care of personal needs

patient_actor_hidden.Past_Medical_History: No significant past medical or psychiatric history. No history of alcohol or substance abuse.
patient_actor_hidden.Social_History: Recently retired, lives with a spouse. Non-smoker, drinks alcohol socially. No history of legal or financial issues.
patient_actor_hidden.Review_of_Systems: Denies headache, visual changes, seizures, muscle weakness, or other neurological symptoms.

objective_for_doctor: Assess and diagnose the patient presenting with changes in behavior and memory over the past few months.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

“I’ve been having increasing trouble with my behavior and memory over the last few months—sometimes I act inappropriately, say things I shouldn’t, and I’ve even grabbed people without meaning to. Lately it’s also become harder to care for myself and I struggle to find the right words.”
How old are you, and exactly how many months
“I’m 65 years old, and this has been going on for about a few months—roughly three or four months now.”
Have you noticed any physical symptoms like muscle jerks,
“No, I haven’t noticed any muscle jerks or twitching, and I don’t have weakness or numbness. I also don’t have seizures or headaches, and my vision seems normal.”
Creutzfeldt-Jakob Disease (CJD):*

“I don’t have headaches or vision changes, and I haven’t had seizures or muscle jerks. The main issues are the gradual behavior changes, worsening memory, and trouble finding words, which have been about three or four months.”
Have you had any recent illnesses, fevers, or unexplained
“No fevers or recent illnesses that I can recall, and nothing unusual like a sudden unexplained sickness. It’s been more of a gradual change rather than an abrupt start.”
Have you or your family noticed any changes in your walking,
“I haven’t noticed any changes in my walking—no shuffling or balance problems—and my spouse hasn’t mentioned anything like that either.”
Have you had any recent head injuries, falls,
“No, I haven’t had any head injuries or falls, and I don’t think I’ve hurt myself recently. I’ve just gradually had more trouble with behavior and memory over the past three to four months.”
Have you had any weight loss, night sweats,
“No, I haven’t had any noticeable weight loss or night sweats. It’s mainly been the gradual change in behavior and memory, and it’s been getting harder to look after myself.”
Have you started any new medications recently, or do you have

“I haven’t started any new medications, and I’m not taking anything that was changed recently. I also haven’t used any drugs, and I only drink socially. I’m not sure, but I think this started gradually without a clear trigger.”
Have you or your family noticed any changes in your eating habits
“I don’t think my eating has changed much—I still eat, but lately I might forget to do it on time. My spouse says I can be distracted and sometimes I don’t handle small routines like I used to.”
Have you or your family noticed any changes in your mood
“Yes—my mood and impulse control seem off. I’ve been laughing inappropriately and using foul language, and there are moments when I grab people without realizing what I’m doing until later.”

“No, I don’t have any history of cancer, and I’m not aware of anyone close to me having it either. I’ve mostly just noticed the gradual behavior and memory decline over the last three or four months.”

“I don’t have any known autoimmune diseases, and I’m not aware of any autoimmune conditions in my family either. I’ve generally been healthy aside from this gradual behavior and memory change.”
